stories.body: Iran launched missile and drone attacks targeting US bases and allied locations in Kuwait, Jordan, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain and Iraq's Kurdistan region following extensive US bombardment of sites across Iran. Kuwait said its military was intercepting an incoming attack. The escalation followed another exchange of threats in which Tehran accused Washington of hitting a wedding party and committing a war crime, while President Donald Trump threatened further strikes and Iran's security chief warned of a new strategy.
stories.headline: Iran strikes US-allied bases as Washington and Tehran trade threats

stories.body: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has fallen sharply amid Iranian attacks and a US naval blockade, disrupting a route vital to Asian oil and gas imports. The crisis has led governments to impose fuel-saving measures and accelerated plans for larger domestic reserves, storage facilities and alternative infrastructure. Japan has announced a $10 billion initiative to help Southeast Asian countries build oil-product supplies, while the Philippines, Thailand and India are pursuing or expanding strategic stockpiles.
stories.headline: Strait of Hormuz disruption cuts shipping traffic and prompts Asia to rethink energy storage

stories.body: NATO and the European Commission pledged support for Germany after Berlin blamed Russia for an attempted explosive-drone attack on a Ukrainian cargo plane at Leipzig/Halle airport. German authorities said the device and its components matched known Russian hybrid operations, while Moscow denied responsibility. Germany announced it would close Russia's consulate in Bonn and a Russian cultural institution in Berlin; Russia responded by saying it would shut Goethe-Institut centres in Moscow, St Petersburg and Yekaterinburg. EU governments are considering further sanctions and restrictions in response.
stories.headline: European allies condemn a new Russian escalation in Germany as Moscow moves to close Goethe-Institut centres

stories.body: China has called on France to abandon a new ultra-fast-fashion law that it says is discriminatory. The measure would impose fees of up to nearly €20 per garment and is aimed at major Asian e-commerce platforms including Shein and Temu. French authorities say the legislation is intended to address the industry's environmental effects and its impact on local businesses.
stories.headline: China condemns France's fast-fashion law targeting major Asian e-commerce platforms

stories.body: A shooting at a downtown Minneapolis apartment building left two people dead and the suspected shooter dead, authorities said. Five people were wounded by gunfire, including two Minneapolis police officers, while a third officer suffered a separate injury. The wounded officers were reported in stable condition as police urged the public to avoid the area.
stories.headline: Minneapolis apartment shooting leaves three dead and wounds two police officers

stories.body: A federal judge in Maryland has issued a preliminary injunction blocking President Donald Trump's latest executive order seeking to limit birthright citizenship. Judge Deborah Boardman said children covered by the class-action case are citizens at birth under Supreme Court precedent. The narrower order had sought to deny automatic citizenship in cases involving birth tourism, people linked to foreign entities and those deemed alien enemies, prompting immigrant families and advocacy groups to argue that it could be applied broadly and arbitrarily.
stories.headline: Judge blocks Trump's renewed attempt to restrict birthright citizenship

stories.body: Elon Musk's America PAC disclosed roughly $800,000 in its first independent expenditures of the 2026 general-election campaign. The group spent on Senate contests in states including Texas, Maine, Ohio, New Hampshire, Iowa, Michigan and Alaska, with its largest outlay directed to Texas, and also backed candidates in eight competitive House races. The spending could add to Republicans' fundraising advantage as Musk considers a substantially larger midterm investment.
stories.headline: Elon Musk's America PAC begins spending in key US House and Senate races

stories.body: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said Spain has no conclusive evidence that Morocco organised the mass crossing into Ceuta at the end of July, while promising to publish government reports on the crisis. The statement came after a police report submitted to a judge described the arrival of more than 70,000 people as planned and raised questions about the conduct of Moroccan security forces. The government says intelligence services did not foresee a crossing on that scale and that the investigation remains open.
stories.headline: Spain's government faces pressure over police report on Morocco's alleged role in the Ceuta mass crossing

stories.body: Opposition leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo demanded that Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez resign or call elections, accusing his government of either incompetence or complicity in the Ceuta crisis. Feijóo argued that Morocco had consented to, and may have coordinated, the mass crossing, and said the government had ignored warning signs. He also raised allegations that Sánchez was reluctant to confront Rabat because of possible information obtained through Pegasus spyware, claims for which he offered no evidence.
stories.headline: Spanish opposition calls for Sánchez to resign over the Ceuta crisis

stories.body: A migrant boat carrying 128 people from Gambia was rescued about 120 kilometres south of Gran Canaria after drifting for 26 days, with only 44 survivors and five bodies aboard. Authorities and aid groups believe more than 80 people, including a baby, died during the journey. Rough seas forced rescuers to leave the bodies on the vessel while they evacuated survivors, several of whom required urgent hospital treatment for severe dehydration, disorientation and other medical problems.
stories.headline: More than 80 people die after a migrant boat drifts south of the Canary Islands for 26 days

stories.body: A judge in Majadahonda has summoned Begoña Gómez, the wife of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, to testify on October 23 in a complaint alleging that she filed a false report against far-right agitator Vito Quiles. Gómez had accused Quiles of harassing and assaulting her at a restaurant in Las Rozas, but a judge dismissed that initial case after reviewing footage and finding no conduct of criminal relevance. Gómez and the Madrid prosecutor's office have appealed the dismissal.
stories.headline: Court summons Begoña Gómez over false-report complaint filed by Vito Quiles

stories.body: An overturned truck closed Barcelona's Ronda del Litoral near Montjuïc in the Llobregat-bound direction during the morning rush hour, causing queues of more than 10 kilometres from Sant Adrià de Besòs. Firefighters worked to stabilise the vehicle and transfer fuel from its tank, while city police diverted traffic and closed entries to the affected carriageway. A fallen streetlight also disrupted freight-train traffic, while a separate truck fire caused delays on the AP-7 near Cerdanyola del Vallès.
stories.headline: Barcelona's Ronda del Litoral is closed after overturned truck causes major rush-hour traffic jams

stories.body: The La Mina consortium is expected to delay pending evictions from the Rambla blocks until December after several flats cleared in June were reoccupied. The 58 occupied homes are needed to relocate residents from the Venus building, which is scheduled for demolition in 2028. Officials suspended planned summer actions after four of 11 evacuated properties were reoccupied and now plan to proceed block by block, alongside increased surveillance, to reduce the risk of immediate reoccupation.
stories.headline: La Mina delays planned evictions from Rambla blocks until December after homes are reoccupied

stories.body: Barcelona's Observatori Fabra recorded a temperature of 33.6°C, its highest September maximum since records began in 1914, surpassing the previous 33.0°C record from 1983. The reading follows the observatory's hottest summer on record, with an average temperature of 27.1°C, 76 days above 30°C and 75 tropical nights. Meteorological data also showed that summer 2026 was the hottest recorded across Catalonia.
stories.headline: Barcelona's Observatori Fabra records its highest September temperature

stories.body: Mossos d'Esquadra have arrested a 28-year-old Turkish fugitive in Barcelona who had been sentenced to 26 years in prison for the attempted shooting murder of two people in Istanbul. He escaped from prison in June while on leave to visit a relative and was wanted under an international arrest warrant. Police tracked him from locations on the Costa Brava to tourist apartments in Barcelona, where he had allegedly relied on two companions to register at accommodation in his place. He is awaiting extradition.
stories.headline: Barcelona police arrest Turkish fugitive convicted over the attempted murder of two people in Istanbul
